attribution: Swami Ramsukhdas; published by Gita Press, Gorakhpur
author: ramsukhdas
summary: A verse-by-verse Hindi commentary on the whole Bhagavad Gita, written for practitioners (sadhakas) rather than scholars.
whyRead: Sadhak Sanjivani is written to be practised, not only studied: it keeps turning each verse into a question about how the reader lives. It is the commentary ingested in this app for all 700 verses, in Hindi and English, so it is the most direct way to go deeper into any Gita verse here.
questions: How do I apply the Gita in ordinary life?
What does it mean to accept that the body is not mine?
How can surrender be practised today?

keyTeachings.title: Written for the practitioner
keyTeachings.text: The title means roughly 'life-giving herb for the spiritual aspirant'. Ramsukhdas repeatedly addresses the reader directly and draws out practical implications of each verse.

keyTeachings.title: Disidentification from body and world
keyTeachings.text: A recurring theme is that the body, mind and possessions belong to the world, not to the Self. Recognising this, in his presentation, is itself a large part of freedom.

keyTeachings.title: Paths are complementary
keyTeachings.text: Ramsukhdas treats action, knowledge and devotion as valid paths suited to different temperaments, while giving surrender (sharanagati) to God a special place.

keyTeachings.title: Service without expectation
keyTeachings.text: Action is to be done for the good of others and offered to God, without seeking anything for oneself. He presents this as available to anyone, regardless of learning.
